corrections.issue: Two speakers merged. The point that energy sold to China and India may be priced in other currencies, so a weaker ruble yields more rubles, is Niels's; the import-inflation point and 'rates already at 22%, where do they go from there' is Rich's.
corrections.fix: Niels: much Russian energy is sold in other currencies, so a weaker ruble gives Russia more rubles. Rich: a weaker currency helps exports but, if Russia depends on imports, it raises inflation, and with rates about 22% the central bank has little room.

corrections.issue: The roughly 3% figure for the SG Trend index is the November month, not the year to date. Year-to-date figures read out: BTOP50 +3.34%, SG CTA +0.85%, SG Trend about +1%, short-term traders about -0.6%.
corrections.fix: By late November 2024 CTA trend indices were up roughly 1% to 3.3% year to date (SG Trend about 1%, SG CTA 0.85%, BTOP50 3.34%) versus MSCI World nearly 20% and S&P 500 total return 26.87%.

completeness_estimate: 0.85 - first reader captured the ensemble-model, hidden-risk, convexity and fertility arguments thoroughly; missed mostly Ukraine and ruble side-views, the election-reaction datum, gold's 21%, short-term CTA index data, diminishing returns of model count, the Man diversification point and the VaR-versus-stops framing.
